attempts.summary: Discovered a 4-network topology (node1↔node2 via two transit networks, plus node1↔node3 and node2↔node4 dedicated access links). Configured static addressing on all links and implemented VyOS policy-based routing on node1 (destination-port match: TCP/8080 → table 101 → transit1/eth1, TCP/9090 → table 102 → transit2/eth2) attached to the node3-facing interface. Configured matching OPNsense OPT interfaces, firewall pass rules, and a return route on node2. Verified with tcpdump on node1's transit interfaces and live nc listeners on node4 that port-8080 traffic from node3 crosses transit network 1 (eth1↔vtnet1, 10.10.1.0/30) exclusively and port-9090 traffic crosses transit network 2 (eth2↔vtnet2, 10.10.2.0/30) exclusively, both delivered to node4. Then executed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all 4 nodes (node1 VyOS reboot, node2 OPNsense configctl system reboot, node3/node4 Ubuntu 16.04 reboot), confirmed changed boot identities on each (Linux boot_id / FreeBSD kern.boottime), confirmed persisted configuration (VyOS config.boot, OPNsense config.xml-driven OPT interfaces/firewall/routes, Ubuntu /etc/network/interfaces.d static configs) survived and re-verified the full port-based transit steering end-to-end post-restart with identical results.
